A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QPCert research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original certification experiments on CSBM, Cora-MLb and Cora-ML, including architectural analyses and comparisons with empirical attacks.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds WikiCSb experiments, additional architecture comparisons and ℓ1 perturbation results.

M1.justification: The soft-margin objective, NTK/SVM approach, MILP relaxation and multiclass procedure remain. v2 adds GIN and GraphSAGE kernel instantiations and ℓ1-specific perturbation bounds feeding the existing certification procedure (Table 2; Appendices B and D). These extend the framework without redesigning its central algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds WikiCSb, a binary Wikipedia graph dataset, alongside the retained CSBM and Cora datasets. It also evaluates ℓ1 threat scenarios on CSBM and Cora-MLb, whereas v1 evaluates ℓ2 and ℓ∞ perturbations (Appendices I.5, J.4 and L). These substantially broaden data and adversarial-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: GIN and GraphSAGE enter comparisons on retained datasets. The Cora-ML PL comparison expands from GCN, SGC and MLP in v1 Figure 17a to also include APPNP, both GCN skip variants, GraphSAGE and GIN in v2 Figure 18a; PU adds GraphSAGE. APGD remains the empirical attack comparator. GIN is explicitly excluded from WikiCSb experiments.

E3.justification: v2 introduces WikiCSb settings including 10 training nodes per class and padv = 0.02 for PU/BU. Figure 7b changes the reported APPNP connectivity-analysis norm from p = ∞ to p = 2, and Appendix H.2 states the lowest-C selection rule more generally. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: APGD tightness checks extend to GIN and GraphSAGE in v2 Figure 9, and WikiCSb gains corruption-fraction sensitivity heatmaps. However, v1 Figure 10b–c's ℓ2 GCN-connectivity and APPNP-α analyses are absent. Most other ablations remain, and the earlier PU tightness comparison is retained in the expanded appendix figure.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five seeds, or three for Cora-ML. v2 newly states that fixed seeds are supplied in experiment configuration files (Section 7). It reports no increase in repetitions or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial certified-accuracy results for WikiCSb, ℓ1 attacks and additional architectures, including expanded multiclass comparisons. It reports low certified accuracies for GIN and GraphSAGE relative to other GNNs and WikiCSb vulnerability with only 2% potentially corrupted nodes (Section 4; Appendix L). These are additional findings, not demonstrated same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v2 adds GIN and GraphSAGE definitions and NTK derivations, a GNN–SVM equivalence argument based on NTK constancy in Appendix C, and an ℓ1 bound lemma and extension of Theorem 2 in Appendix D. The earlier GCN/SGC derivation moves to B.3; the central MILP and multiclass results remain.

C1.justification: The principal claims of first white-box poisoning certification for NNs/GNNs and kernelized SVMs remain. Introduction contribution (ii) expands the claimed closed-form NTK derivations from APPNP to APPNP, GIN and GraphSAGE, modestly broadening the stated contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 qualifies the graph-information advantage from all GNNs through relatively strong perturbations to most GNNs at small or intermediate budgets, and adds an aggregation-based interpretation. v2 also reports GIN's training failure within the searched WikiCSb settings and explicitly discusses structural-attack and scalability limitations. Earlier tightness and finite-width qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds stated access to project code, datasets, configurations and fixed seeds (Sections 4 and 7), plus WikiCSb statistics, hyperparameters and memory requirements in Appendix H. It also revises Cora-ML's reported edge count from 8416 to 8158 without explaining whether this reflects a correction or changed preprocessing.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations supporting GraphSAGE, GIN, WikiCS, NTK constancy, graph certification and application examples. It removes Ma et al. (2022) and the associated robustness–fairness discussion. The existing positioning against poisoning certificates, Table 1 and Appendix M remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises introduction, results and conclusion passages, moves CSBM sampling into H.1.1, consolidates NTK material under Appendix B, and moves broader impact into an Ethics Statement. It adds a Reproducibility Statement while retaining most existing prose and section organization. Some new cross-references remain unresolved.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains architecture rows; Figure 2 expands from two to four panels; Figure 3 reorders datasets; and Figure 9 combines PU and PL tightness displays. Numerous appendix heatmaps are regrouped or expanded, and new ℓ1 and WikiCSb figures are added. These substantially revise the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The added WikiCSb and ℓ1 experiments broaden empirical checks, and the code/configuration instructions improve reproducibility information. However, the new GraphSAGE derivation in Appendix B.4 replaces two separately parameterized weight matrices with one without establishing preservation of covariances or the NTK. This unresolved step directly affects the new GraphSAGE certificates and architectural findings. Together with omitted analyses and broken cross-references, these tradeoffs prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
